# fortiappseccloud_waf_known_attacks

Configures known attacks for one FortiAppSec Cloud application using the static app endpoint `/waf/apps/{ep_id}/known_attacks`. Set `template = false` and provide `configs` to manage settings directly. Set `template = true` and omit `configs` to inherit this module from the application's attached WAF template.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_known_attacks` resource for an application endpoint. Template-level settings are managed by `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_known_attacks`.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_known_attacks" "example" {
  ep_id    = fortiappseccloud_waf_app.example.ep_id
  template = false

  configs {
    status            = true
    sensitivity_level = 2
    action            = "alert_deny"
    cross_site_script = true
    sql_inject        = true
    trojans           = true

    # Omit this ownership wrapper to preserve the complete remote
    # sig_except_rules array. Keep the wrapper but remove every item block
    # to explicitly send [].
    sig_except_rules {
      item {
        sig_id   = "030000010"
        sig_name = "SQL Injection"
        cookie {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "sessionid"
        }
        host {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "www.example.com"
        }
        http_header {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "X-Example"
        }
        json {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "data"
        }
        param {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "query"
        }
        url {
          status = true
          type   = "regex"
          value  = "^/admin"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Import

Import using the application `ep_id`:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_known_attacks.example application-endpoint-id
```

The first read after import hydrates all ownership wrappers when `template = false`.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
